basic_info: 58-year-old male presenting with chest pain and shortness of breath following a fall
present_illness: Onset of chest pain and shortness of breath after a fall, leading to emergency room admission. The chest pain was described as a pressure feeling in the middle of the chest, lasting a few minutes, without radiation, sweating, or nausea, accompanied by shortness of breath. The patient tripped and fell, not recalling the exact mechanism of injury, and did not hit his chest or back directly. He did not lose consciousness and continued walking until he started feeling out of breath. No swelling or bruising on chest or back noted post-fall. Shortness of breath resolved with walking. No palpitations, dizziness, or syncope reported. No prior cardiac conditions reported. No history of coronary artery disease, heart attack, or arrhythmias. No prior cardiac evaluations or imaging mentioned. The patient was not specifically evaluated for thoracic spine or chest injuries during the ER visit.
past_history: No prior cardiac conditions reported. No history of coronary artery disease, heart attack, or arrhythmias. No prior cardiac evaluations or imaging mentioned. The patient is aware of having hypertension.
physical_exam: Vital signs: Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 78 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Cardiac examination: No jugular venous distension, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Respiratory examination: Clear breath sounds bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdominal and extremity examinations unremarkable.
aux_exam: Echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular function, no pericardial effusion, no valvular abnormalities, mild to moderate mitral regurgitation. Chest X-ray: No evidence of rib fractures or pneumothorax. ECG: Normal sinus rhythm, no ST-segment changes or Q waves. Troponin levels: Within normal limits. No imaging performed for thoracic spine or chest injuries during ER visit per patient report.
